items.quote: Held Strong: Maine, Ohio (late surge really helped), Texas (again strong late rural surge), Michigan, Wisconsin

election_day_reports.text: 32.9% of active registered voters had voted before polls opened (by 5 AM MT), up from 31.2% Monday morning; 750,469 early in person.
Fayette County (Lexington) 19,187 Election Day votes by 6:28 AM MT; Secretary of State Michael Adams says 438,602 voted early vs 313,009 in 2023 (an off-year governor race, not a midterm).

map_notes: States not listed in races are shown grey (no tracked Senate race on this site).
takeaways_summary: Compared with the 2022 midterm, early voting is mixed with a slight tilt toward Democrats, at low confidence, and the final pre-Election Day numbers didn't change that. North Carolina's early ballots lean more Democratic than in 2022 (checked against the state's own file), and in Texas turnout grew faster in Democratic-leaning counties than in Republican-leaning ones. Iowa leans less Democratic than 2022, and Maine looks about the same. Early votes are not results: many Republicans vote on Election Day, and unaffiliated voters decide close races.

takeaways.headline: Michigan: about a third of active voters had already voted when polls opened
takeaways.detail: State data show 32.9% of Michigan's active registered voters had cast ballots by 7 AM ET Tuesday, including 750,469 early in-person votes; 2,313,165 ballots had been cast as of Monday morning. Michigan doesn't register by party, so this is turnout, not direction.
takeaways.source_label: CBS Detroit citing Michigan state data

takeaways.headline: North Carolina's final early vote: registered Democrats up 12.25 points
takeaways.detail: The state's own file shows 2,828,288 accepted ballots: 1,085,329 from registered Democrats, 738,750 Republicans and 995,435 unaffiliated, a 12.25-point Democratic edge versus about 7.0 at the same point in 2022 (tracker). Registration isn't vote choice.
takeaways.source_label: NC State Board of Elections absentee file

takeaways.headline: Iowa's final early vote still leans less Democratic than 2022
takeaways.detail: 498,713 early ballots, with registered Democrats ahead by 10.7 points versus 17.5 at the same point in 2022. Volume is up 35%.
takeaways.source_label: Call the Map (Iowa Secretary of State data)

takeaways.headline: Florida: Republicans' pre-Election Day ballot lead is smaller than in 2022
takeaways.detail: Registered Republicans led mail and early ballots by 133,177 (2,176,256 R vs 2,043,079 D of 5,408,792) per the Division of Elections on Nov 2, versus about 300,000 in 2022 per the Miami Herald. Election Day in-person voting, which leans Republican, is still under way. This is turnout by registration, not votes.
takeaways.source_label: FL Division of Elections via floridapredictions.com; Miami Herald

takeaways.headline: Trader odds: Democrats about 76-78% to win the Senate
takeaways.detail: Kalshi 76%, Polymarket 78% for Democratic Senate control as of 8:03 AM MT. Iowa is near a coin flip (52-53%). These are trader odds, not a forecast or a call.

takeaways.headline: Overall: mixed, tilting slightly toward Democrats compared with 2022
takeaways.detail: North Carolina and Texas lean toward Democrats compared with 2022, Iowa leans toward Republicans, and Maine looks about the same. Kansas, Michigan, Ohio, Alaska and South Carolina have no like-for-like 2022 comparison. This is turnout, not votes.
takeaways.source_label: NC State Board of Elections; Texas SOS via early.professorbutts.com; Call the Map

takeaways.headline: Texas: early voting grew faster in Democratic-leaning counties than in Republican-leaning ones
takeaways.detail: In the 8 counties Democrats won by 20+ points, early votes are up 47.6% from 2022 (1.29 million vs 876,000). In the 221 counties Republicans won by 20+ points, they're up 34.0% (2.27 million vs 1.69 million). Statewide, 7.72 million voted early, up 40.5% from 2022 but down 14.8% from 2024. Texas has no party registration, so this compares places, not voters.
takeaways.source_label: Texas Secretary of State county early-vote data, compiled by early.professorbutts.com

takeaways.headline: North Carolina early ballots lean more Democratic than in 2022 (checked against the state's file)
takeaways.detail: The state's own file shows 2,819,922 accepted early ballots. Registered Democrats lead registered Republicans by 12.2 points, compared with a 6.9-point Democratic lead at the same point in 2022, per the Call the Map tracker. About 1 million ballots came from unaffiliated voters, who could go either way.
takeaways.source_label: North Carolina State Board of Elections absentee file

takeaways.headline: South Carolina's final early vote: 1,043,810 ballots
takeaways.detail: In-person early voting ended Oct 31 with 1,043,810 ballots, per the state election commission. South Carolina has no party registration, and no comparable 2022 county figures were available, so this doesn't show a direction.

takeaways.headline: Iowa early ballots lean less Democratic than in 2022
takeaways.detail: Among about 464,000 early ballots, registered Democrats lead by 12.3 points, down from an 18.7-point Democratic lead at the same point in 2022. Total early ballots are up 36% from 2022.

takeaways.headline: Maine early ballots look about the same as 2022
takeaways.detail: Registered Democrats lead among about 295,000 early ballots by 24.1 points, close to the 25.5-point Democratic lead in 2022.

takeaways.headline: Party registration is not the same as votes
takeaways.detail: These numbers count which party early voters are registered with, not who they voted for. Since 2020 many Republicans have shifted to voting on Election Day, so early ballots often lean Democratic and Election Day ballots lean Republican. Early leads in the count can shrink or grow as more votes come in.

takeaways.headline: First polls close Tuesday at 4:00 PM MT
takeaways.detail: Most of Indiana and eastern Kentucky close first at 4:00 PM MT on Nov 3; North Carolina and Ohio close at 5:30 PM MT; Iowa at 7:00 PM MT; most of Alaska at 10:00 PM MT.
takeaways.source_label: Midterm Results Live poll closing times

takeaways.headline: Some states give turnout only, with no party breakdown
takeaways.detail: Michigan, Ohio, Texas, South Carolina and Alaska report how many people voted early but not their party. For Texas, county-level turnout is used instead; for the others, no direction can be read yet.

left.paraphrase: Early vote turnout is about 20% above 2022, with a surge among young voters and voters of color; he says Election Day reads should be adjusted 2-3 points toward Democrats because independents have swung their way.
left.author: Simon Rosenberg (@SimonWDC)
left.fact_check: Partly supported. Turnout is up versus 2022 (Texas +40.5%, Florida pace +8.2% per On Point). The demographic surge and the 2-3 point independent adjustment are his own estimates and can't be checked.

left.paraphrase: North Carolina's early vote is 12.8 points more Democratic than 2024 and 4.9 points more than 2022, pointing to a strong Democratic showing.
left.author: On Point Politics (@onpointpolitics)
left.fact_check: Broadly consistent with the data: the state file shows a 12.2-point Democratic registration edge, about 5 points more than 2022 and 13 more than 2024 per the tracker. Their Senate forecast is their own, and registration isn't vote choice.

right.paraphrase: Florida Election Day in-person voting is running ahead of the same time in 2024 for Republicans, with rural counties strongest; she says Florida never looked in danger, and the real test is whether the Senate holds, which she puts as possible in a D+8 or better environment.
right.author: DataRepublican (@DataRepublican)
right.fact_check: Unverifiable for now: the comparison uses her own minute-by-minute 2024 snapshots, and the state doesn't publish live Election Day totals in a comparable form. The pre-Election Day data shows the Republican ballot lead (133,177) is smaller than 2022's (about 300,000), so a strong Republican Election Day is needed to match past margins.

right.paraphrase: Republicans held strong in early voting in Maine, Ohio, Texas and Michigan, with late rural surges.
right.author: Election2026 Updates (@MadAboutSkin01)
right.fact_check: Partly supported. Maine is close to 2022. Ohio and Michigan don't report party, so it can't be checked. In Texas, Republican-leaning counties grew 34% vs 2022 but Democratic-leaning counties grew faster (48%).
